record.paper_title: Selected Conjectures and Open Problems on Directed Graphs
record.context_brief: maximum directed cuts in acyclic digraphs
record.original_question: For acyclic digraphs with m arcs, let h(m) be the minimum, over all such digraphs, of the maximum size of a directed cut, where a directed cut (X, Y) consists of all arcs from X to Y. What is the infimum alpha_0 of alpha > 0 such that h(m) = m/4 + O(m^alpha) for all m >= 1?

evidence.quote: For directed graphs, the directed cut (X, Y ) is the set of arcs from X to Y .
Corresponding to g(m), we can define a function h(m) for all acyclic digraphs with m arcs.
Problem 5.1 What is the infimum α0 of α > 0 such that, for m ≥ 1, h(m) = m 4 +O(mα)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An acyclic digraph is a finite directed graph with no directed cycles. For a digraph $D=(V,A)$ and a partition $V=X\sqcup Y$, the directed cut $(X,Y)$ is the set of arcs of $D$ with tail in $X$ and head in $Y$; its size is $|(X,Y)|$. For an acyclic digraph $D$, let $\mathrm{mc}(D)$ denote the maximum of $|(X,Y)|$ over all partitions $V=X\sqcup Y$. Define
$$h(m)=\min\{\mathrm{mc}(D): D\text{ is an acyclic digraph with exactly }m\text{ arcs}\}.$$
It is known that $h(m)=m/4+o(m)$. Determine
$$\alpha_0=\inf\{\alpha>0 : h(m)=\tfrac{m}{4}+O(m^{\alpha})\text{ as }m\to\infty\}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: The exact value of α₀ remains open. Work of Alon, Bollobás, Gyárfás, Lehel and Scott (J. Graph Theory, 2007) establishes the bounds α₀ ∈ [3/5, 4/5] for acyclic digraphs, but no improvement determining the precise infimum is known.

status_evidence.title: Maximum directed cuts in acyclic digraphs
status_evidence.snippet: Every digraph with m edges has a directed cut of size at least m/4; bounds give α₀ ∈ [3/5, 4/5].
status_evidence.claim: Best known bounds place α₀ between 3/5 and 4/5, with the exact value undetermined.
